title: fleet.task.v1
description: A unit of work the orchestrator can hand to one agent: one repo, one branch, one worktree (docs/agent-fleet.md principle 5). Everything an agent is permitted to touch and everything the orchestrator will check afterwards is declared here, up front, rather than discovered from the agent's own narration (docs/fleet.md).

id.description: Unique task identifier, e.g. 'R2.11', 'CI-4', 'ROOT-DOC-1'. Unique across fleet/tasks/ (checked by fleet.py validate, not by this schema alone, since uniqueness is a cross-file property).

title.description: One-line human-readable summary of the task.

repo.description: Which repo the agent runs in: the workspace root, or one of the two service submodules (AGENTS.md repo map). An agent assigned here edits only that repo (AGENTS.md section 3).

base.description: Branch this task's branch is created from. Defaults to 'main' when omitted; fleet.py applies the default, the schema only documents it.

branch.description: Branch name the agent commits to, inside its own worktree (AGENTS.md section 5: one agent = one worktree = one branch).

needs.description: Dependencies that must hold before this task can start. Every need's 'task' MUST resolve to either another id in fleet/tasks/ or an entry in fleet/external.json -- there is no longer an implicit 'unknown id, trust it' fallback. fleet.py plan reads the referenced external.json entry's own hand-maintained 'state' to decide readiness; the need's own 'state' here just records what this task's author believes it needs.

allowed_paths.description: Glob patterns, relative to this task's repo root, naming every path the agent may create or modify. Must be relative with no '..' segment and no absolute/drive prefix -- enforced by fleet.py's check_path_safety, not by this schema's pattern (kept loose here so each failure mode -- absolute vs '..' -- is independently mutation-tested as its own Python check). The orchestrator diffs the agent's commits against this list after the run (allowed_paths_violations in result.v1.json); fleet.py plan additionally checks that same-repo, same-layer tasks do not claim overlapping globs, and that no open fleet/external.json item claims an overlapping path in the same repo.

acceptance.description: Commands the orchestrator itself runs after the agent hands back control -- never the agent's own say-so (docs/fleet.md: agents are untrusted narrators).

prompt_file.description: Path, relative to the workspace root, to this task's prompt (fleet/prompts/<id>.md). Same relative-path safety rule as allowed_paths, enforced by fleet.py. fleet.py validate also checks the file exists.

model.description: Model identifier or capability tier (docs/agent-fleet.md section 2) the agent runs on.

max_turns.description: Hard cap on agent turns for this task, enforced by the orchestrator, not the agent.

risk.description: Coarse blast-radius classification used to decide review depth and serialization caution. 'docs' = prose only, 'ci' = pipeline/workflow config, 'code' = application source.

notes.description: Free-text operational cautions a human author wants attached to the task -- e.g. an explicit 'must not run concurrently with X' that isn't (yet) mechanically enforced. fleet.py never acts on these; they are read by the orchestrator/human scheduling the run. Mechanically-enforced overlaps belong in allowed_paths/needs/fleet/external.json instead.

agent.description: Which herdr pane/CLI this task is meant to run under (docs/agent-fleet.md roles; the fuller per-pane CLI/fencing design lives in the historical .fleet/panes.md note). Optional: a task without it is assumed to run on whatever pane the orchestrator's default assigns for its risk tier.

task.description: Id of the task this depends on. Must match a fleet/tasks/ id or a fleet/external.json key -- fleet.py validate fails otherwise.

state.description: 'pushed' = the dependency's branch has been pushed by the orchestrator (not yet merged); 'merged' = it has landed on its base branch. For an external.json dependency, the actual readiness fact comes from that entry's own 'state' field, not from this claim.

name.description: Short label for this check, shown in result.v1.json acceptance_results.

cwd.description: Directory the command runs in, relative to the task's repo root ('.' for the repo root itself).

command.description: Shell command the orchestrator runs verbatim. Never the agent.

expect_exit.description: Exit code that counts as a pass for this check.

pane.description: Role/pane name this task runs under, e.g. 'Developer', 'Test Author', 'Contract Owner' (docs/agent-fleet.md section 3).

cli.description: Which CLI/model family the pane runs. Concrete model names live in that CLI's own config, reviewed quarterly (docs/agent-fleet.md principle 4) -- never hardcoded here.

fresh_context.description: True for reviewer-style panes that must start every run with no prior chat history (docs/agent-fleet.md principle 3: author != reviewer).
